thread.title: Must-Read Scorecard For The 30 Stocks Of The Dow

author: Richard Henry Suttmeier
title: Must-Read Scorecard For The 30 Stocks Of The Dow
text:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell into correction territory last week but did not stay there thanks to new all-time intraday highs for Apple and Visa on Friday. The Dow ended last week at 24,262.22, down 1.8% year-to date and 8.8% below its all-time intraday high of 26,616.71 set on Jan 26.
The following nine tickers set new 2018 lows during the first four days of May: DIS, GS, IBM JNJ, KO, MMM, PG, TRV and UTX. IBM, KO and PG are members of the "Dogs of the Dow" for 2018 .
Here’s the Dow 30 Scorecard
Global Market Consultants Scorecard For The Dow 30
Note that four stocks are in bear market territory: General Electric, 3M, Procter & Gamble and Wal-Mart.
Fourteen components are in correction territory. Only five components have double-digit year-to-date gains : Boeing, Cisco Systems, Intel, Microsoft and Visa. The Weekly Chart For The Dow
Courtesy of MetaStock Xenith Courtesy of MetaStock Xenith
The weekly chart for the Dow is neutral with the stock below its five-week modified moving average of 24,398.43. The 12x3x3 weekly slow stochastic reading rose to 33.01 last week, up from 31.01 on April 27. Stocks Above Their Five-Week Modified Moving Average
Apple (AAPL) ended last week above its five-week modified moving average of $171.77 and has a positive weekly chart. American Express (AXP) ended last week above its five-week modified moving average of $96.76 and has a positive weekly chart. Cisco Systems (CSCO) ended last week above its five-week modified of $43.66 and has a positive weekly chart. Cisco reports first quarter results after the close on May 16. Chevron (CVX) ended last week above its five-week modified of $120.65 and has a positive weekly chart. Home Depot (HD) ended last week above its five-week modified of $180.94 and has a positive weekly chart. Home Depot reports first quarter results before the open on May 16. Intel (INTC) ended last week above its five-week modified of $51.03 and has a positive weekly chart. McDonald’s (MCD) ended last week above its five-week modified of $160.79. Merck (MRK) ended last week above its five-week modified of $56.97 and has a positive weekly chart. Microsoft (MSFT) ended last week above its five-week modified of $93.40 and has a positive weekly chart. Nike (NKE) ended last week above its five-week modified moving average of $67.22 and has a positive weekly chart. UnitedHealth (UNH) ended last week above its five-week modified moving average of $229.94 with a positive weekly chart. Visa (V) ended last week above its five-week modified of $123.18 and has a positive weekly chart.
